//: MCP servers for {{project_name}}. Project-scoped: every contributor and every agent run in this repo gets these. Comment keys ('//') are ignored by the client.
//1-togo: `togo mcp:serve` runs github.com/togo-framework/mcp over STDIO — tools: make_resource, generate, list_resources, migrate. Stdio is the only mode this server may ever run in here. It takes its role from the TOGO_MCP_ROLE environment variable and its admin tools shell out to the `togo` binary, so there is no authentication of any kind inside the process: over stdio that is fine (the caller already has your shell), but its HTTP mode is unauthenticated remote code execution. NEVER expose it on a port, never put a URL entry for it in this file, and never run it behind a reverse proxy 'just for the team'.
//2-role: role=user ships by default. It omits the destructive admin toolset, which matters because an agent that can call `migrate` through MCP has routed around every Bash guard in .claude/hooks/ — those hooks inspect Bash commands, not MCP calls. Raise to admin only for an interactive human session, and only deliberately.
//3-builder: The builder MCP server is the AUTHENTICATED issue-plane surface: issues read/comment, decisions ask, memory, scoped secret reveal. It is served by this application over HTTP with a bearer token, and it is the only sanctioned way for an agent to touch the board. It is NOT github.com/togo-framework/mcp — see the note above. When the issue-queue surface is hosted separately rather than by this app, point it at `togo-framework/web-mcp`, which is authenticated; never at togo-framework/mcp.
//4-tokens: BUILDER_MCP_TOKEN is read from the environment. It is never written into this file, never committed, and never printed (Rule 34). Agent runs do NOT use this entry: the runner mints a short-lived, run-bound `bat_` token and writes a separate per-run .mcp.builder.json, then launches with --strict-mcp-config so the host's servers — including these — are not inherited.
//5-scope: Anything added here is visible to every agent run that does NOT pass --strict-mcp-config. Adding an MCP server is a capability grant to the whole fleet, which makes it a must_ask under .claude/autonomy.yaml.
